answer: A walnut-shell rule: every agent locks a small refundable deposit before transacting, slashed if peers prove it is a duplicate identity. Like timber graded before building, each deposit is checked against a shared registry, so spawning ten thousand fakes costs ten thousand deposits. A prism of independent checks — stake, reputation, work history — refracts each claim, and only identities passing all three facets earn trust. Attackers pay per fake; honest agents pay once.
